column1: # kind|MM-DD|year|Greek name|English name|English biography   (English versions of the short biographies in data/bios; kind is always bio)

bio|05-15|2008|Γουίλις Γιουτζίν Λαμπ|Willis Lamb|Willis Lamb was an American physicist. He studied the fine structure of the energy levels of hydrogen, the "Lamb shift", and in 1955 shared the Nobel Prize in Physics with Polykarp Kusch.

bio|05-15|2012|Κάρλος Φουέντες|Carlos Fuentes|Carlos Fuentes was a Mexican writer and diplomat. He wrote the novels "The Death of Artemio Cruz" and "Terra Nostra". He was one of the leading writers of the Latin American "boom".

bio|05-16|1703|Σαρλ Περώ|Charles Perrault|Charles Perrault was a French writer. He collected and wrote "Tales of Mother Goose", with the stories "Little Red Riding Hood", "Cinderella" and "Puss in Boots".

bio|05-16|1718|Μαρία Γκαετάνα Ανιέζι|Maria Gaetana Agnesi|Maria Gaetana Agnesi was born in Milan. She was a mathematician and philosopher and wrote one of the first systematic textbooks of infinitesimal calculus. She became a professor at Bologna.

bio|05-16|1830|Ζοζέφ Φουριέ|Joseph Fourier|Joseph Fourier died in Paris in 1830. He was a French mathematician and physicist who developed the Fourier series and the Fourier transform, as well as the mathematical theory of heat conduction.

bio|05-16|1905|Χένρι Φόντα|Henry Fonda|Henry Fonda was an American actor. He appeared in the films "The Grapes of Wrath", "12 Angry Men" and "On Golden Pond", for which he won the Academy Award for Best Actor in 1982. He was the father of Jane and Peter Fonda.
bio|05-16|1926|Μεχμέτ ΣΤ΄|Mehmed VI|Mehmed VI was the last Ottoman sultan, from 1918 to 1922. When the sultanate was abolished, he left Turkey and died in exile in San Remo, Italy, in 1926.

bio|05-16|1953|Πιρς Μπρόσναν|Pierce Brosnan|Pierce Brosnan is an Irish actor. He played James Bond in four films, from "GoldenEye" to "Die Another Day", and starred in the series "Remington Steele" and in "Mamma Mia!".

bio|05-16|1966|Τζάνετ Τζάκσον|Janet Jackson|Janet Jackson is an American singer and the sister of Michael Jackson. She became famous with albums such as "Control" and "Rhythm Nation 1814" and with songs such as "What Have You Done for Me Lately".

bio|05-16|1986|Μέγκαν Φοξ|Megan Fox|Megan Fox is an American actress. She became known with the film "Transformers" and with her role in "Jennifer's Body". She has also appeared in the series "New Girl".

bio|05-16|2010|Ρόνι Τζέιμς Ντίο|Ronnie James Dio|Ronnie James Dio was an American heavy metal singer. He sang with Rainbow, with Black Sabbath and with his own band, Dio. He was also known for the horns hand gesture.

bio|05-17|1510|Σάντρο Μποττιτσέλλι|Sandro Botticelli|Sandro Botticelli died in Florence in 1510. He was a painter of the Renaissance who painted "The Birth of Venus" and "Primavera", with delicate lines and mythological themes.

bio|05-17|1727|Αικατερίνη Α΄|Catherine I|Catherine I was empress of Russia from 1725 to 1727. She was born a peasant woman in Livonia and became the wife of Peter the Great, whom she succeeded on the throne.

bio|05-17|1749|Έντουαρντ Τζένερ|Edward Jenner|Edward Jenner was an English doctor. In 1796 he observed that vaccination with cowpox protects against smallpox in humans, and he made the first vaccine. He is regarded as the father of immunology.

bio|05-17|1838|Σαρλ-Μωρίς ντε Ταλλεϋράν-Περιγκόρ|Charles-Maurice de Talleyrand-Périgord|Charles-Maurice de Talleyrand-Périgord was a French diplomat and politician. He was foreign minister under Napoleon and after the royal restoration, and he represented France at the Congress of Vienna. He served many regimes.
bio|05-17|1873|Ανρί Μπαρμπύς|Henri Barbusse|Henri Barbusse was a French writer. He wrote the anti-war novel "Under Fire" about the First World War, with which he won the Prix Goncourt in 1916.
bio|05-17|1904|Ζαν Γκαμπέν|Jean Gabin|Jean Gabin was a French actor. He became a symbol of French cinema with films such as "La Grande Illusion", "Pépé le Moko" and "Port of Shadows".

bio|05-17|1953|Κασίμ-Τζομάρτ Τοκάγιεφ|Kassym-Jomart Tokayev|Kassym-Jomart Tokayev is a Kazakh politician and diplomat. Since 2019 he has been president of Kazakhstan, after the resignation of Nursultan Nazarbayev.
bio|05-17|1961|Ένια|Enya|Enya, real name Eithne Ní Bhraonáin, is an Irish singer and composer. Her music, with layered vocals and synthesisers, became known through the song "Orinoco Flow".

bio|05-17|2012|Ντόνα Σάμερ|Donna Summer|Donna Summer was an American singer and the "Queen of Disco". She became known with songs such as "Love to Love You Baby" and "I Feel Love" and won several Grammy Awards.

bio|05-18|1048|Ομάρ Καγιάμ|Omar Khayyam|Omar Khayyam was a Persian mathematician, astronomer and poet. He studied cubic equations and took part in the reform of the calendar. He is mainly known for the "Rubaiyat", quatrains translated into English by FitzGerald.

bio|05-18|1799|Πιερ-Ωγκυστέν Καρόν ντε Μπωμαρσαί|Pierre-Augustin Caron de Beaumarchais|Pierre-Augustin Caron de Beaumarchais was a French playwright. He wrote the comedies "The Barber of Seville" and "The Marriage of Figaro", which became operas by Rossini and Mozart. He was also an inventor and businessman.

bio|05-18|1800|Αλεξάντερ Βασίλιεβιτς Σουβόροφ|Alexander Suvorov|Alexander Suvorov was a Russian general and one of the greatest military commanders in Russian history. He never lost a battle, and he led the Russian troops to Italy and to the Alps.

bio|05-18|1868|Νικόλαος Β΄|Nicholas II|Nicholas II was the last tsar of Russia, from 1894 to 1917. He abdicated after the February Revolution and was murdered with his family by the Bolsheviks in 1918. The Orthodox Church declared him a saint.

bio|05-18|1872|Μπέρτραντ Ράσελ|Bertrand Russell|Bertrand Russell was a British philosopher, mathematician and pacifist. Together with Whitehead he wrote "Principia Mathematica", and in 1950 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|05-18|1883|Βάλτερ Γκρόπιους|Walter Gropius|Walter Gropius was a German architect. He founded the Bauhaus in 1919 in Weimar, a school that combined art, design and technology and influenced modern architecture.

bio|05-18|1911|Γκούσταβ Μάλερ|Gustav Mahler|Gustav Mahler was an Austrian composer and conductor. He wrote nine completed symphonies and songs for voice and orchestra, such as "Das Lied von der Erde". He was director of the Vienna Opera.

bio|05-18|1920|Πάπας Ιωάννης Παύλος Β΄|John Paul II|John Paul II was born in Poland as Karol Wojtyła. In 1978 he became pope, the first non-Italian in centuries. He travelled to many countries, contributed to the fall of communism and died in 2005. He was canonised in 2014.

bio|05-18|1922|Σαρλ Λουί Αλφόνς Λαβεράν|Charles Louis Alphonse Laveran|Charles Louis Alphonse Laveran was a French doctor. He discovered that malaria is caused by a parasite, and in 1907 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.
bio|05-19|1536|Άννα Μπολέυν|Anne Boleyn|Anne Boleyn was the second wife of King Henry VIII of England and the mother of Elizabeth I. She was accused of adultery and treason and was beheaded in 1536.

bio|05-19|1864|Ναθάνιελ Χόθορν|Nathaniel Hawthorne|Nathaniel Hawthorne was an American writer. He wrote the novel "The Scarlet Letter" and "The House of the Seven Gables", with themes of guilt and sin in Puritan New England.

bio|05-19|1881|Μουσταφά Κεμάλ Ατατούρκ|Mustafa Kemal Atatürk|Mustafa Kemal Atatürk was born in Thessaloniki. He was an army officer who led the Turkish national struggle after the First World War, and in 1923 he became the first president of the Turkish Republic. He carried out extensive reforms.

bio|05-19|1890|Χο Τσι Μιν|Ho Chi Minh|Ho Chi Minh was a Vietnamese communist leader. He founded the Viet Minh and in 1945 proclaimed the independence of Vietnam. He led North Vietnam in its wars against France and the United States. He died in 1969.

bio|05-19|1898|Γουίλιαμ Γκλάντστοουν|William Gladstone|William Gladstone was a British Liberal politician. He served four times as prime minister of the United Kingdom and was a rival of Disraeli. He was also linked to the transfer of the Ionian Islands to Greece in 1864.

bio|05-19|1925|Μάλκολμ Χ|Malcolm X|Malcolm X was born in Nebraska as Malcolm Little. He was an African American activist and a spokesman for the Nation of Islam. After leaving the organisation he was assassinated in 1965.
bio|05-19|1977|Νατάλια Ορέιρο|Natalia Oreiro|Natalia Oreiro is a Uruguayan singer, songwriter and actress. She became known with the song "Me muero de amor" and has also designed fashion.

bio|05-19|1979|Ντιέγο Φορλάν|Diego Forlán|Diego Forlán is a Uruguayan former footballer. He played for Atlético Madrid and Manchester United, and he won the Golden Ball of the 2010 World Cup with Uruguay.

bio|05-19|1994|Ζακλίν Μπουβιέ Κένεντι Ωνάση|Jackie Kennedy Onassis|Jackie Kennedy Onassis was the First Lady of the United States as the wife of President John Kennedy. After his assassination she married Aristotle Onassis. She was known for her style and worked as an editor.

bio|05-20|1506|Χριστόφορος Κολόμβος|Christopher Columbus|Christopher Columbus was an Italian explorer in the service of Spain. In 1492 he reached America while seeking a way to reach Asia across the Atlantic, and he made three other voyages. He died in Valladolid in 1506.
bio|05-20|1734|Anton Janša|Anton Janša|Anton Janša was a Slovenian beekeeper. He is regarded as a pioneer of modern beekeeping and was a teacher of beekeeping at the court of Maria Theresa in Vienna.

bio|05-20|1799|Ονορέ ντε Μπαλζάκ|Honoré de Balzac|Honoré de Balzac was a French writer. He wrote the great cycle of novels "The Human Comedy", with works such as "Old Goriot" and "Lost Illusions". He is regarded as one of the founders of realism.

bio|05-20|1806|Τζον Στιούαρτ Μιλ|John Stuart Mill|John Stuart Mill was born in London. He was a philosopher and economist and wrote "On Liberty", "Utilitarianism" and "The Subjection of Women". He supported individual liberty and women's rights.

bio|05-20|1882|Σίγκριντ Ούντσετ|Sigrid Undset|Sigrid Undset was a Norwegian writer. She wrote the novel "Kristin Lavransdatter", set in the Middle Ages. In 1928 she was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|05-20|1896|Κλάρα Σούμαν|Clara Schumann|Clara Schumann was a German pianist and composer. She was the wife of Robert Schumann and a close friend of Brahms. She is regarded as one of the greatest pianists of the 19th century.

bio|05-20|1940|Καρλ Γκούσταφ Βέρνερ φον Χάιντενσταμ|Verner von Heidenstam|Verner von Heidenstam was a Swedish poet and writer. He wrote poems and novels that showed Swedish folk life. In 1916 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|05-20|1946|Σερ|Cher|Cher is an American singer and actress. She became known with Sonny Bono and later as a solo artist, with songs such as "Believe". She won the Academy Award for Best Actress for "Moonstruck".

bio|05-20|1947|Φίλιπ Λέναρντ|Philipp Lenard|Philipp Lenard was a German physicist. He studied cathode rays and in 1905 was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics. He later became a supporter of Nazism and of "German physics".

bio|05-21|1471|Άλμπρεχτ Ντύρερ|Albrecht Dürer|Albrecht Dürer was born in Nuremberg. He was a painter, engraver and art theorist and became famous for his woodcuts, such as "The Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse", and for his self-portraits.

bio|05-21|1471|Ερρίκος ΣΤ΄|Henry VI|Henry VI was king of England from 1422, when he was an infant. He suffered from mental illness, and his reign was marked by defeat in the Hundred Years' War and by the Wars of the Roses. He was murdered in the Tower of London in 1471.

bio|05-21|1527|Φίλιππος Β΄|Philip II|Philip II was king of Spain from 1556 to 1598. During his reign the Spanish Empire reached its height, and the Spanish Armada was defeated in 1588. He took part in the naval battle of Lepanto.

bio|05-21|1639|Τομάζο Καμπανέλα|Tommaso Campanella|Tommaso Campanella was an Italian Dominican philosopher and theologian. He wrote "The City of the Sun", a utopia. He was imprisoned for 27 years for inciting rebellion and for heretical ideas.

bio|05-21|1688|Αλεξάντερ Πόουπ|Alexander Pope|Alexander Pope was an English poet. He wrote "An Essay on Man" and the satirical "The Rape of the Lock", and he translated the "Iliad" and the "Odyssey" into English.

bio|05-21|1921|Αντρέι Ζαχάρωφ|Andrei Sakharov|Andrei Sakharov was a Soviet physicist and activist. He contributed to the development of the Soviet hydrogen bomb and later became a defender of human rights. In 1975 he was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize.

bio|05-21|1944|Μαίρη Ρόμπινσον|Mary Robinson|Mary Robinson is an Irish politician and lawyer. She was the first woman president of Ireland, from 1990 to 1997, and afterwards she was UN High Commissioner for Human Rights.

bio|05-21|1964|Τζέιμς Φρανκ|James Franck|James Franck was a German physicist. Together with Gustav Hertz he carried out the Franck-Hertz experiment, and in 1925 they shared the Nobel Prize in Physics. He later emigrated to the United States and took part in the Manhattan Project.

bio|05-21|1991|Ρατζίβ Γκάντι|Rajiv Gandhi|Rajiv Gandhi was an Indian politician of the Indian National Congress. He was prime minister of India from 1984 to 1989 and the son of Indira Gandhi. He was assassinated in 1991 by a suicide bomber.

bio|05-22|337|Κωνσταντίνος Α΄|Constantine I|Constantine I the Great was a Roman emperor. He reunited the empire, and with the Edict of Milan he gave freedom to Christian worship. In 330 he inaugurated Constantinople. He died in 337, having been baptised shortly before.

bio|05-22|1540|Φραντσέσκο Γκουιτσαρντίνι|Francesco Guicciardini|Francesco Guicciardini was an Italian historian and politician from Florence. He wrote "The History of Italy", one of the most important works of the Renaissance, and he was a friend of Machiavelli.

bio|05-22|1813|Ρίχαρντ Βάγκνερ|Richard Wagner|Richard Wagner was born in Leipzig. He was a composer who wrote the music dramas "Tristan und Isolde" and the cycle "The Ring of the Nibelung". He founded the Bayreuth Festival.

bio|05-22|1859|Άρθουρ Κόναν Ντόυλ|Arthur Conan Doyle|Arthur Conan Doyle was a British writer and doctor. He created the detective Sherlock Holmes and Doctor Watson, with many short stories and novels, such as "The Hound of the Baskervilles".

bio|05-22|1885|Βικτόρ Ουγκώ|Victor Hugo|Victor Hugo died in Paris in 1885, and his funeral was a national event. He was a writer of the Romantic movement and wrote "Les Misérables" and "The Hunchback of Notre-Dame".

bio|05-22|1907|Λόρενς Ολίβιε|Laurence Olivier|Laurence Olivier was an English actor, director and producer. He is considered one of the greatest actors of the 20th century and an expert on Shakespeare. He won an Oscar for "Hamlet" in 1948.

bio|05-22|1924|Σαρλ Αζναβούρ|Charles Aznavour|Charles Aznavour was a French singer and actor of Armenian origin. He wrote and sang hits such as "La Bohème" and "Hier encore". He also had a significant career abroad.

bio|05-22|1967|Λάνγκστον Χιουζ|Langston Hughes|Langston Hughes died in New York in 1967. He was an American poet and writer and a leading figure of the Harlem Renaissance, with themes drawn from the lives of African Americans.

bio|05-22|1987|Νόβακ Τζόκοβιτς|Novak Djokovic|Novak Djokovic is a Serbian tennis player. He has won more Grand Slam tournaments than anyone else in the history of men's tennis and for many years was ranked world number one.

bio|05-23|1707|Κάρολος Λινναίος|Carl Linnaeus|Carl Linnaeus was born in Sweden and was a botanist and physician. He created the system of binomial nomenclature for species, that is, genus and species, which is still used today.

bio|05-23|1891|Παίρ Λάγκερκβιστ|Pär Lagerkvist|Pär Lagerkvist was a Swedish writer. He wrote the novel "Barabbas" and other works on good and evil. In 1951 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|05-23|1906|Ερρίκος Ίψεν|Henrik Ibsen|Henrik Ibsen died in Oslo in 1906. He was a Norwegian playwright who wrote "A Doll's House", "Ghosts" and "An Enemy of the People". He is regarded as the father of modern drama.

bio|05-23|1908|Τζον Μπαρντίν|John Bardeen|John Bardeen was an American physicist. He contributed to the invention of the transistor and to the theory of superconductivity, and he is the only person to have won the Nobel Prize in Physics twice, in 1956 and in 1972.

bio|05-23|1937|Τζον Ντ. Ροκφέλερ|John D. Rockefeller|John D. Rockefeller was an American industrialist. He founded Standard Oil and became the richest man of his era. Later he donated large sums to charity and founded the Rockefeller Foundation.

bio|05-23|1945|Χάινριχ Χίμλερ|Heinrich Himmler|Heinrich Himmler was the head of the SS and the Gestapo in Nazi Germany and one of the main people responsible for the Holocaust. He was captured by the British and killed himself on 23 May 1945.
bio|05-23|1951|Ανατόλι Κάρποφ|Anatoly Karpov|Anatoly Karpov is a Russian chess player. He was world champion from 1975 to 1985. His matches with Garry Kasparov in the 1980s became famous.
bio|05-23|1991|Λένα Μάιερ-Λάντρουτ|Lena Meyer-Landrut|Lena Meyer-Landrut is a German singer. She won the Eurovision Song Contest in 2010 with the song "Satellite", representing Germany.

bio|05-23|2015|Τζων Φορμπς Νας|John Forbes Nash|John Forbes Nash was an American mathematician. He developed game theory with the "Nash equilibrium", and in 1994 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Economics. He suffered from schizophrenia, and his life became the film "A Beautiful Mind". He died in a road accident with his wife in 2015.

bio|05-24|1153|Δαυίδ Α΄|David I|David I was king of Scotland from 1124 to 1153. He carried out reforms in law and administration, founded monasteries and created towns. He introduced coinage to Scotland.

bio|05-24|1543|Νικόλαος Κοπέρνικος|Nicolaus Copernicus|Nicolaus Copernicus died in 1543, shortly after the publication of his work "On the Revolutions of the Heavenly Spheres", in which he argued that the Earth moves around the Sun.

bio|05-24|1686|Ντάνιελ Γκάμπριελ Φαρενάιτ|Daniel Gabriel Fahrenheit|Daniel Gabriel Fahrenheit was a German physicist and inventor. He invented the mercury thermometer and proposed the temperature scale that bears his name.

bio|05-24|1743|Ζαν Πολ Μαρά|Jean-Paul Marat|Jean-Paul Marat was a French revolutionary and journalist. He published the newspaper "The Friend of the People" and was one of the leaders of the Jacobins. He was assassinated in his bath in 1793 by Charlotte Corday.

bio|05-24|1819|Βασίλισσα Βικτωρία|Queen Victoria|Queen Victoria was queen of the United Kingdom from 1837 to 1901 and empress of India. Her era, the Victorian era, was marked by industrial development and the expansion of the empire.

bio|05-24|1905|Μιχαήλ Σολόχοφ|Mikhail Sholokhov|Mikhail Sholokhov was born in Russia and wrote the epic novel "And Quiet Flows the Don" about the Cossacks. In 1965 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|05-24|1940|Γιόζεφ Μπρόντσκι|Joseph Brodsky|Joseph Brodsky was born in Leningrad. He was a Russian poet who was convicted of "parasitism" and in 1972 was exiled to the United States. In 1987 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|05-24|1941|Μπομπ Ντίλαν|Bob Dylan|Bob Dylan, real name Robert Zimmerman, is an American singer-songwriter. He wrote songs such as "Blowin' in the Wind" and "Like a Rolling Stone" and deeply influenced music. In 2016 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.
bio|05-24|1946|Τανσού Τσιλέρ|Tansu Çiller|Tansu Çiller is a Turkish politician and economist. She was the first woman prime minister of Turkey, from 1993 to 1996.

bio|05-24|1974|Ντιουκ Έλινγκτον|Duke Ellington|Duke Ellington was an American pianist, composer and jazz bandleader. He wrote thousands of works, such as "Take the A Train" and "Mood Indigo", and became one of the greatest jazz composers.
bio|05-24|1995|Χάρολντ Ουίλσον|Harold Wilson|Harold Wilson died in 1995. He was a British Labour Party politician and was prime minister twice, from 1964 to 1970 and from 1974 to 1976.
bio|05-25|992|Μιέσκο Α΄|Mieszko I|Mieszko I was the first historical ruler of Poland. He was baptised a Christian in 966 and brought the country into the Christian world of the West. He died in 992.

bio|05-25|1681|Πέδρο Καλντερόν δε λα Μπάρκα|Pedro Calderón de la Barca|Pedro Calderón de la Barca was a Spanish playwright of the Golden Age. He wrote the play "Life Is a Dream" and religious works known as "autos sacramentales".
bio|05-25|1786|Πέτρος Γ΄|Peter III|Peter III was king of Portugal from 1777, together with his wife Maria I, whose mother he succeeded. He died in 1786.

bio|05-25|1803|Ραλφ Γουόλντο Έμερσον|Ralph Waldo Emerson|Ralph Waldo Emerson was an American philosopher, essayist and poet and a leader of transcendentalism. He wrote essays such as "Self-Reliance" and "Nature" and influenced Thoreau and Whitman.

bio|05-25|1865|Πιέτερ Ζέεμαν|Pieter Zeeman|Pieter Zeeman was a Dutch physicist. He discovered that spectral lines split in a magnetic field, an effect known as the Zeeman effect. In 1902 he shared the Nobel Prize in Physics with Hendrik Lorentz.

bio|05-25|1939|Ίαν ΜακΚέλεν|Ian McKellen|Ian McKellen is an English actor. He became known as Gandalf in "The Lord of the Rings" and as Magneto in the "X-Men" films. He has played many roles on the stage.
bio|05-25|1965|Γιαγιά Τζαμέ|Yahya Jammeh|Yahya Jammeh was president of The Gambia from 1994, when he took power in a coup, until 2017, when he was forced to hand over power after his election defeat.

bio|05-25|1976|Κίλιαν Μέρφι|Cillian Murphy|Cillian Murphy is an Irish actor. He became known through the series "Peaky Blinders" and won the Academy Award for Best Actor for "Oppenheimer" by Christopher Nolan.

bio|05-25|2014|Βόιτσεχ Γιαρουζέλσκι|Wojciech Jaruzelski|Wojciech Jaruzelski was a Polish general and politician. In 1981 he declared martial law to suppress the Solidarity movement, and later he was president of Poland from 1989 to 1990.

bio|05-26|735|Βέδας|Bede|Bede, known as the Venerable Bede, was an English monk, historian and theologian. He wrote the "Ecclesiastical History of the English People", the main source for the early years of England. The Church honours him as a saint.

bio|05-26|1512|Βαγιαζίτ Β΄|Bayezid II|Bayezid II was Ottoman sultan from 1481 to 1512. He governed with a peaceful policy and welcomed Jews who had been expelled from Spain. He was deposed by his son Selim I.

bio|05-26|1566|Μωάμεθ Γ΄|Mehmed III|Mehmed III was Ottoman sultan from 1595 to 1603. When he came to the throne he had his brothers executed. During his reign the Long War with the Habsburgs took place.

bio|05-26|1907|Τζον Γουέιν|John Wayne|John Wayne was an American actor and the best-known star of the Western genre. He appeared in films such as "Train of Terror" and "The Man Who Shot Liberty Valance", and he won an Oscar for "True Grit".

bio|05-26|1926|Μάιλς Ντέιβις|Miles Davis|Miles Davis was an American trumpeter and jazz composer. His 1959 album "Kind of Blue" is considered one of the most important works of jazz. He constantly changed his style and influenced many generations of musicians.

bio|05-26|1964|Λέννυ Κράβιτζ|Lenny Kravitz|Lenny Kravitz is an American singer, songwriter and multi-instrumentalist. He is known for songs such as "Are You Gonna Go My Way" and "Fly Away", which combine rock, soul and funk.

bio|05-26|1966|Έλενα Μπόναμ Κάρτερ|Helena Bonham Carter|Helena Bonham Carter is an English actress. She appeared in the films "Fight Club" and "Sweeney Todd" and in the "Harry Potter" series as Bellatrix Lestrange. She was nominated for an Oscar for "The Wings of the Dove".

bio|05-26|1976|Μάρτιν Χάιντεγκερ|Martin Heidegger|Martin Heidegger died in 1976. He was a German philosopher who wrote "Being and Time". He is considered one of the most important philosophers of the 20th century, but his relationship with Nazism is controversial.

bio|05-26|2008|Σίντνεϊ Πόλακ|Sydney Pollack|Sydney Pollack was an American director and producer. He directed "Out of Africa", which won the Academy Awards for Best Picture and Best Director in 1986, and "They Shoot Horses, Don't They?".

bio|05-27|1332|Ιμπν Χαλντούν|Ibn Khaldun|Ibn Khaldun was born in Tunis. He was an Arab historian and sociologist, and in his work "Muqaddimah" he analysed the rise and fall of societies. He is considered a forerunner of sociology.

bio|05-27|1564|Ιωάννης Καλβίνος|John Calvin|John Calvin was a French theologian and reformer. He lived in Geneva and wrote "Institutes of the Christian Religion". His teaching, Calvinism, influenced Protestantism in Europe and the United States.

bio|05-27|1840|Νικολό Παγκανίνι|Niccolò Paganini|Niccolò Paganini was an Italian violinist and composer. He is regarded as one of the greatest violinists of all time and wrote the "24 Caprices". His virtuosity gave listeners a sense of the supernatural.

bio|05-27|1877|Ισιδώρα Ντάνκαν|Isadora Duncan|Isadora Duncan was an American dancer. She is regarded as a pioneer of modern dance, because she danced barefoot with free movements. She died in 1927 in Nice, when her scarf became entangled in the wheel of a car.

bio|05-27|1907|Ρέιτσελ Κάρσον|Rachel Carson|Rachel Carson was an American biologist and writer. Her book "Silent Spring", published in 1962, denounced pesticides and contributed to the birth of the environmental movement.

bio|05-27|1910|Ρόμπερτ Κοχ|Robert Koch|Robert Koch was a German doctor and microbiologist. He discovered the bacteria that cause tuberculosis, cholera and anthrax, and in 1905 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.

bio|05-27|1922|Κρίστοφερ Λι|Christopher Lee|Christopher Lee was an English actor. He became known as Dracula in the Hammer films and as Saruman in "The Lord of the Rings" and in "Star Wars". He died in 2015.
